sentences.text: A semiconductor diode is formed by joining P-type and N-type silicon.
It acts as a one-way valve for electric current.
When forward-biased (anode more positive than cathode), standard silicon diodes conduct with a constant forward voltage drop of approximately 0.7 Volts.
When reverse-biased, the diode blocks current completely up to its breakdown voltage.
Four diodes configured in a Full-Wave Bridge Rectifier convert alternating AC current into pulsating direct DC current.
